gap: No result ChatGPT got works out, for a single blanket at the US DOE's typical 60 W, the hours each 1 kWh station runs once its own AC draw is included, or the cost per usable Wh: the BLUETTI AC180 gives 13.1 h at $0.51 per usable Wh and the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 gives 12.4 h at $0.57 per usable Wh, both at $499.
standout_why: I compared runtimemath.com, blackoutwise.com, wattfort.com, testedwatts.com and our own page. runtimemath adds the station's own draw only for BLUETTI models, and only at 100 W and 200 W. Blackoutwise uses 75 W with no own-draw term. WattFort recommends no stations and has no prices. TestedWatts adds a flat 10 W and gives no prices. None gives cost per usable Wh or runtimes at the 60 W single-blanket figure with each station's own draw included. Part of this (own draw added to the load) is already on runtimemath, so 1, not 2.
decides: This confirms the AC180 over the Elite 100 V2. They cost the same $499 on bluettipower.com today, and the AC180 runs about 0.7 h longer on a 60 W blanket with a lower cost per usable Wh. Both cover a 10 h night at 60 W, but neither covers 10 h at 100 W (8.5 h and 7.9 h). The Elite 30 V2 runs only about 3.5 h on a 60 W 120 V blanket, so it belongs only with low-draw 12 V blankets. The AC180 is now listed as available, which corrects our page's 'back late Nov' stock note.
